title: The Vacuus and the Resonus: Form and Emptiness in the Planes of Polyhedra

subjects.term: MSC2020 52C35: Arrangements of points, flats, hyperplanes

description:
Take a polyhedron P with a centre O inside it. Its Vacuus is the set of planes through O and an edge of P (DICTO, #87 and #110); its Resonus is the set of planes through O parallel to a face of P. The Vacuus follows the edges, the Resonus follows the faces, and both are read off the polar P*: each Vacuus plate is at right angles to an edge of P* and each Resonus plane is at right angles to the line from O to a corner of P* (Theorem 4, a direct consequence of polarity). For a zonotope the Resonus is a known arrangement, the adjoint of its hyperplane arrangement (Aguiar and Mahajan); on the permutohedron it is the resonance arrangement of Shadrin, Shapiro and Vainshtein, the restricted all-subset arrangement of Kamiya, Takemura and Terao (Theorem 5); and for the truncated icosidodecahedron its 31 planes are Buckminster Fuller's 31 great circles. We give both frameworks exactly and side by side for 163 catalogue rows (159 distinct polyhedra): the 5 Platonic, 13 Archimedean and 13 Catalan polyhedra, the uniform prisms and antiprisms with n = 3 to 12 and their polars, the bipyramids and trapezohedra, and all 92 Johnson polyhedra about two centres, every count in exact arithmetic. The Vacuus is of the heart kind exactly when P is centrally symmetric (#110; Theorem 1); its Resonus counterpart rests on Minkowski's theorem, and in the catalogue fails only for the truncated tetrahedron (Theorem A). The rhombic dodecahedron and the rhombic triacontahedron are the only polyhedra of the catalogue whose Vacuus and Resonus are the same planes. On the permutohedron the plates of the ridges and their number A402191 are those of #105; here they follow from the standard pencil lemma (Theorems 2 and 3), with the type-B count (5n − 2·3n + 1)/2 (Theorem 3B). Two laws decide when a Resonus plane or a Vacuus plate is a mirror (Theorems 6 and 7), and the 120-cell is the only regular polytope of dimension at least 2 whose Resonus is its whole mirror arrangement (Theorem 8); we found no earlier statement of these. The 360 walls of the 600-cell in #110, whose 60 and 300 directions are Waegell and Aravind's, are named here as the Resonus of the 600-cell and the Resonus of the 120-cell. Read in the other direction, the same planes fix the empty regions they leave and the Betti numbers of their complexified complement through one polynomial (Zaslavsky; Orlik and Solomon); we give both exactly for every Vacuus and Resonus of the catalogue and for the permutohedra (Theorem 9).

Version 2 adds Lean names for Theorems 1 (one direction), 2, 3, 4 and 5, with Theorems 3 and 5 from the Palomar-registered entry PALOMAR-2026-11-27-000010; Section 7.5, the lattice-web test (Theorem 10); one line on the polar of the true Vacuus (§7.1); a first paragraph saying what is known and what is new; and Figure 2, all four of DICTO's Vacuus builds as exact renders. No result of Version 1 changes.
